newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crime cost S.African Telkom 775 mln rand in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Crime cost S.African Telkom 775 mln rand in 96/97.

text.p: South Africa's Telkom communications utility lost at least 775 million rand to theft and fraud in the 1996/97 financial year, Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo said on Wednesday.
Replying to a question in parliament, he said copper cable to the value of 40 million rand was stolen, an 80 percent increase on the previous year's losses.
Naidoo said that when loss of income and other costs were included, the theft of cable represented an estimated total loss of 250 million rand to Telkom in financial 1996/97.
When fraud and associated losses were added, the total rose to a "best scenario" of 775 million rand and a worst case of 1.0 billion rand.
Last month, the South African government closed a deal selling a 30 percent stake in Telkom to a consortium of U.S.-based SBC Communications Inc and Telekom Malaysia Bhd for $1.26 billion.
